A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MT-RAIG benchmark and evaluation framework. Their complete main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–E support reliable comparison; the appendices are textually and visually identical.

before.justification: v1 reports original retrieval and insight-generation experiments, human validation, and meta-evaluation in Tables 3–6, plus appendix ablations and case studies.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results, including the main benchmark comparisons and all appendix analyses.

M1.justification: The benchmark construction pipeline and MT-RAIG EVAL procedures are unchanged, including table-aware claim decomposition, question-aware topic decomposition, verification, matching, and appendix prompts.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same 18,532-example benchmark constructed from SPIDER and Open-WikiTable, covering joinable and topic-related tables and the same four question types. No evaluated domain or test scenario changes.

E2.justification: The same five retrievers, eleven generators, and seven baseline evaluation metrics participate in the corresponding main and appendix comparisons. The newly cited VerifiNER work is not evaluated as a baseline.

E3.justification: DPR top-10 retrieval, gold-table comparisons, the 300-sample human validation, and the 250-pair meta-evaluation remain unchanged. Appendix B retains the same model checkpoints, training settings, and inference procedures.

E4.justification: Figure 5 retains the analyses of retrieval count, irrelevant-table noise, and gold-table count. Appendix C retains evaluator-backbone and model-size studies, and Appendix E retains the same case studies.

E5.justification: Human agreement and Cohen’s kappa reporting in Table 3, along with the correlation estimation procedures, are unchanged. v3 adds no run-count, seed, uncertainty, or significance-testing information.

E6.justification: Numerical results, rankings, plotted trends, and qualitative examples are unchanged throughout. For example, DPR Recall@10 remains 80.83 in Table 4, and MT-RAIG EVAL’s correlations remain 64.94 and 67.67 in Table 5. Table 6 changes only a caption label.

T1.justification: The task formulation and faithfulness/completeness definitions in Equations 1–3 are unchanged. Neither version adds or revises formal assumptions, derivations, or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: a multi-table retrieval-augmented insight benchmark, a decomposition-based evaluator, and evidence that existing models struggle with the task.

C2.justification: Result interpretations and substantive limitations remain unchanged. v3 adds a generic hallucination warning in Ethical Consideration; v1 already discusses unfaithful synthetic responses and unreliable LLM judgments, so this introduces no substantive new limitation or applicability boundary.

D1.justification: The first-page resource address changes from a GitHub repository to a GitHub Pages project address. This changes the documented access point; the PDFs do not establish a change in resource availability. Implementation details and prompts remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v3 adds VerifiNER (Kim et al., 2024b) as support for the hallucination caveat. Related-work discussion and novelty positioning remain unchanged. Other Kim citation suffixes shift, and shortened bibliography author lists do not remove cited works.

P1.justification: v3 makes limited wording and spelling edits, updates an author’s email, adds a funding acknowledgement, and abbreviates long bibliography author lists. The overall section structure and scientific narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: Table 6’s caption corrects A&R to A&S, matching Table 2 and the existing column headings. The acknowledgement and bibliography edits cause limited layout reflow. Figures, table structures, and appendix displays remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: The corrected Table 6 caption and abstract typos provide small local improvements, while the acknowledgement, citation, and project-address updates improve documentation only modestly. The scientific argument, experimental evidence, implementation guidance, and substantive limitations remain unchanged, supporting no meaningful net difference in overall paper quality.
